classification.difficultyReason: Compare three supplied candidates across five groups, infer missing angles or3-4-5 sides, track ordered correspondences and choose the congruence test. Multiple linked familiar deductions and representation matching, no unsignposted auxiliary proof.

content.prompt: In each part, find a pair of congruent triangles. State the congruence test used.

spec.description: Three upright triangles in source order ABC, PQR, XYZ. Ordinary source-blue outlines are black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AB=XY=3 cm; AC=XZ=5 cm; angle BAC=angle YXZ=35 degrees. PQ=3 cm, PR=5 cm, angle QPR=40 degrees.

answer.worked:
$AB=XY=3\text{ cm}$, $AC=XZ=5\text{ cm}$ and $\angle BAC=\angle YXZ=35^\circ$.

The equal angle is included between the equal sides, so $\triangle BAC\equiv\triangle YXZ$ (SAS).

spec.description: Two upright isosceles triangles followed by an inverted isosceles triangle. Matching ticks are local to each figure; all ordinary marks are black.
spec.mathematics: AB=BC, AC=4 cm, angle BAC=50 degrees; PQ=QR=4 cm, angle QPR=50 degrees; XZ=YZ, XY=4 cm, angle XZY=80 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Derived angles are absent from the question figure.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle XZY$ (AAS).

Use equal base angles and the triangle angle sum.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=BC$, so $\angle BCA=50^\circ$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=180^\circ-50^\circ-50^\circ\\\angle ABC&=80^\circ\end{align*}$$

In $\triangle XYZ$, $XZ=YZ$.

$$\begin{align*}\angle ZXY&=\frac{180^\circ-80^\circ}{2}\\\angle ZXY&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$

Thus $\angle BAC=\angle ZXY=50^\circ$, $\angle ABC=\angle XZY=80^\circ$ and $AC=XY=4\text{ cm}$. Hence $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle XZY$ (AAS).

spec.description: Three separate right triangles with original orientations, right-angle squares and all numerical givens. Ordinary outlines and marks are black.
spec.mathematics: ABC: right angle B, AB=3 cm, AC=5 cm. PQR: right angle Q, PR=5 cm, QR=4 cm. XYZ: right angle Y, ZY=5 cm, YX=3 cm.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PQR$ (SSS).

Pythagoras gives $BC=4\text{ cm}$ and $PQ=3\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}BC^2&=AC^2-AB^2\\BC^2&=5^2-3^2\\BC^2&=16\\BC&=4\text{ cm}\\PQ^2&=PR^2-QR^2\\PQ^2&=5^2-4^2\\PQ^2&=9\\PQ&=3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

Therefore $AB=PQ=3\text{ cm}$, $BC=QR=4\text{ cm}$ and $AC=PR=5\text{ cm}$. Hence $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle PQR$ (SSS).

spec.description: Three candidate triangles. The middle triangle retains only its printed angle and side; no equality ticks are invented. Ordinary marks are black.
spec.mathematics: CA=AB=20 mm and angle CAB=40 degrees; angle RPQ=70 degrees and RQ=20 mm; XY=20 mm, angle YXZ=40 degrees and angle XZY=70 degrees.

answer.worked:
Since $CA=AB$, the base angles of $\triangle ABC$ are equal.

$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC&=\frac{180^\circ-40^\circ}{2}\\\angle ABC&=70^\circ\\\angle XYZ&=180^\circ-40^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle XYZ&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$

Thus $\angle CAB=\angle YXZ=40^\circ$, $\angle ABC=\angle XYZ=70^\circ$ and $AB=XY=20\text{ mm}$. Hence $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle XYZ$ (AAS).

spec.description: Three candidates with distinct 12 cm side positions. The final baseline extends beyond Z to retain the exterior angle. Ordinary marks are black.
spec.mathematics: ABC: AB=12 cm, angle ABC=43 degrees, angle BCA=20 degrees. PQR: RQ=12 cm, angle RPQ=43 degrees, angle PQR=20 degrees. XYZ: ZY=12 cm, angle XYZ=20 degrees, exterior angle at Z=63 degrees.

answer.short:
$\triangle PQR\equiv\triangle XYZ$ (AAS).

The exterior angle gives $\angle YXZ=43^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Using the exterior angle of $\triangle XYZ$:

$$\begin{align*}\angle YXZ&=63^\circ-20^\circ\\\angle YXZ&=43^\circ\end{align*}$$

Now $\angle RPQ=\angle YXZ=43^\circ$, $\angle PQR=\angle XYZ=20^\circ$ and $QR=YZ=12\text{ cm}$. Hence $\triangle PQR\equiv\triangle XYZ$ (AAS).
